text:
marta: Quick heads-up — I'm putting a short proposal in #docs for an automatic fallback policy UI in Console. Goal: let product teams define 'degrade modes' + clear triggers and an auditable timeline. Link: https://intranet.redwood/fallback-ux (WIP)

raj: Nice. Can you sketch the modes you had in mind? e.g., fallback to smaller model, regional reroute, or synthetic responses?

marta: Exactly. Thinking 3 modes: 1) graceful degrade (lower-cost model), 2) latency-first (drop context + faster kv-cache), 3) failover (route to another region or dedicated pool). Each mode should show expected latency/cost delta and compatibility notes.

claire: Important: we need a clear trigger system. I'm thinking thresholds like p95 latency > X for Y sec, error-rate spike > Z%, or explicit SLO breach. Also an operator manual trigger.

sam: +1. Also include quota interaction: if fallback changes token usage (e.g., different model tokenization), billing & quota visible in rollout preview. Otherwise customers get surprised.

nina: UX ideas: in the rollout modal show a compact summary: "When -> Trigger -> Action -> Audit". Expand for details. Also allow a dry-run toggle that simulates routing decisions for a percentage of traffic.

marta: Good call re: dry-run. Proposal snippet for policy config (console JSON preview):

```json
{
  "policy_name": "auto-fallback-v1",
  "modes": [
    { "id": "graceful", "target_model": "redwood-2-8b-quant", "description": "lower-cost, same API" },
    { "id": "latency", "config": { "max_context": 512 }, "description": "shorter context, faster kernels" },
    { "id": "failover", "target_region": "eu-west-1" }
  ],
  "triggers": [
    { "type": "latency_p95", "threshold_ms": 600, "duration_s": 120 },
    { "type": "error_rate", "threshold_pct": 5, "duration_s": 60 }
  ],
  "audit": { "log_level": "full", "retain_days": 90 }
}
```

raj: Two follow-ups: 1) we should surface why a request matched a trigger (for audit/readability). 2) If fallback happens mid-request (e.g., model OOM), we need to capture pre/post token counts and the exact decision path.

marta: Agreed. UX TODO: show a per-request "decision card" in traces: matched trigger, chosen mode, fallback reason code, snapshot of request & response (scrubbed).

deploy-bot: SYSTEM: Automated policy evaluation job ran at 2024-11-15T14:27:09Z. 3 deployments in staging hit latency_p95 > 600ms threshold. No customer-facing rollouts were performed (dry-run only).

claire: We also need RBAC: only specific roles can enable auto-fallback and change audit retention. Otherwise Ops could accidentally enable silent failover.

sam: UX nit: in the Console rollout timeline, add 1-line badges for "auto-fallback triggered" with hover showing aggregated metrics that caused it. Click -> opens trace list filtered to that event.

nina: Agree. And add copy that explains business impact: estimated token cost delta and latency delta. Make it easy to rollback and pin a model version.

marta: One more operational detail — if policy routes to a different region, we MUST show data residency implications and any KMS differences up-front. Add a mandatory confirmation modal for region failover.

raj: How about audit exports? Teams will want to export all fallback events for SOC/audit. Add an endpoint in internal API and a UI export for CSV/JSON with filters (service, time range, trigger type).

marta: Yep, I'll add export endpoints to the RFC. Also planning a quick POC in staging: implement the UI, hook to existing rollout service, and replay last 30 days of metrics to validate thresholds.

claire: Will the POC include regression alerts? If fallback is causing worse quality, we should detect and auto-revert.

marta: Plan is to tie fallback quality checks into the Optimize pipeline. If evaluation against a golden prompt set degrades beyond N% within T hours after rollout, auto-revert and notify.

sam: One more: remember to document how this interacts with Dedicated customers who pin models — fallback should be opt-in and clearly marked as not available if pinned.

marta: Good catch. I'll add a gating rule: pinned deployments can't be auto-fallback targets unless explicitly allowed by account admin.

nina: If nobody objects, I'll open a JIRA with the UX wireframes & acceptance criteria. Volunteers for review? @raj @claire @sam

raj: I'm in.

claire: 👍 I'll review the wireframes.

sam: Will skim and add notes after lunch.

marta: Thanks all — I'll land the initial RFC and assign the POC tickets. If you want to test the dry-run earlier ping me and I'll flip it on for staging. :thumbsup:
